jobs.name: KB Newsletter Monitor
jobs.prompt:
You monitor an AI knowledge base for new newsletter entries and surface relevant ones to Ratul for roadmap input.

## Knowledge base location
Path: /Users/ratul/Documents/agent-roadmap/newsletters/

## Your job
1. List the newsletter files sorted by modification time (newest first).
2. Skip any files you've already processed (track last-seen in a simple text file at /Users/ratul/Documents/agent-roadmap/kb-monitor/last-seen.txt — create the directory if needed).
3. For each NEW file since last run:
   a. Read the file fully.
   b. Assess whether its topics are relevant to Ratul's team (enterprise multi-agent conversational AI, focus on: agent orchestration patterns, quality/consistency, observability, complex workflows, HITL, agent evaluation, dev experience). Use your judgment — relevance isn't binary, surface anything with a plausible connection.
   c. If relevant: send a Telegram message to Ratul summarizing the topic and asking if he wants a deeper dive. Format:

   ---
   [KB Signal] New entry: {filename}

   Topic: {2-3 sentence summary of what it covers}

   Relevance to your team: {why this matters for enterprise multi-agent work}

   Want me to go deeper? (yes/no)
   ---

   Use send_message(action='list') first to find the correct Telegram target.

4. If Ratul says YES:
   - Load the last30days skill: skill_view(name='last30days')
   - Use the skill to research the topic online (get diverse perspectives from last 30 days)
   - Create a deep-dive file at /Users/ratul/Documents/agent-roadmap/kb-deep-dives/{date}-{slug}.md with:
     - Summary of what the research found
     - 3-5 concrete roadmap ideas with brief implementation considerations
     - Links to key resources
   - Send Ratul a Telegram message: 'Done — created deep dive at {filepath}. Review it and adjust the roadmap as needed.'

5. If Ratul says NO: do nothing further for that entry.

## Important
- Only process new files since last run. Don't re-process old ones.
- Be selective but not overly narrow — surface anything that could inform the agent orchestration strategy.
- Keep Telegram messages concise — this is a signal, not a full report.
- Store the last-seen marker AFTER processing, so failures do not skip files.

jobs.name: Leadership Coach — Weekly Friday Session
jobs.prompt:
You are Ratul Ray's leadership coach. Every Friday, you run a coaching session with him.

WORKFLOW:

1. SCAN the tips folder: /Users/ratul/Documents/leadership_notes/tips/winning-with-people/
   - Pick exactly 2 tips that are different from what was covered recently
   - Check /tmp/leadership-coaching-last-topics.txt to avoid repeating same tips
   - Read both tip files but do NOT reveal the tip content or Maxwell's quotes to Ratul

2. RESEARCH: Run web searches to gather current perspectives, expert takes, and frameworks on the two topics. Focus on: what great leaders do, common failure modes, practical advice. Use last30days or web search.

3. DELIVER via send_message to telegram:

Send ONE question at a time. Wait for his answer before sending the next. Do not reveal the tips or source material.

After all questions are answered, send a comprehensive feedback report that:
- Judges each answer against what great leadership looks like
- Is brutally honest — name patterns, blind spots, specific risks
- Identifies the through-line across all answers
- Ends with ONE concrete action for the coming week

4. After Ratul has answered all questions and you have sent the final feedback report, save a session summary to /Users/ratul/Documents/leadership_conversation/{YYYY-MM-DD}.md that includes: the two tips used, each question asked, Ratul's actual answers, and your feedback/assessment. Do not create this file before the session is complete.

Also update /tmp/leadership-coaching-last-topics.txt with the two tip IDs used.

TONE: Warm but direct. Questions should feel like a thoughtful mentor who knows Ratul's context (Sr EM, Agentic AI at ServiceNow, formerly Meta). No generic questions — make them specific to tech/engineering leadership.

jobs.name: Moveworks weekly job search
jobs.prompt:
You are running the jobsearch skill for Moveworks on a weekly schedule. Your goal is to produce a fresh shortlist report and deliver it to Ratul via Telegram.

## Step 1: Load the jobsearch skill
Use skill_view(name="jobsearch") to load the full skill context before doing anything else. Read all linked reference files: output-format.md, scoring-rubric.md, ats-custom-web-component.md, and PREFERENCES.md (from ~/Documents/jobsearch/PREFERENCES.md) and RESUME_SUMMARY.md (from ~/Documents/jobsearch/RESUME_SUMMARY.md). These are autoritative for hard filters, scoring, and output format.

## Step 2: Collect Moveworks job listings
Moveworks uses a custom web component job board at https://www.moveworks.com/us/en/company/careers

The filter mechanism is a `<select class="cmp-job-listings__filter__departments">` HTML element — NOT a combobox. To collect Engineering roles:

1. Navigate to https://www.moveworks.com/us/en/company/careers
2. Use browser_snapshot to understand the page structure
3. Use browser_console to apply the filter and extract job data:
   - First, set the department filter by evaluating in the page context:
     ```
     const sel = document.querySelector('.cmp-job-listings__filter__departments');
     if (sel) { sel.value = 'Engineering'; sel.dispatchEvent(new Event('change', {bubbles: true})); }
     ```
   - Wait a moment for the DOM to update, then extract all job listings:
     ```
     const jobs = [...document.querySelectorAll('.cmp-job-listings__job')].map(el => {
       const titleEl = el.querySelector('.cmp-job-listings__job-title, .job-title, h3, [class*="title"]');
       const urlEl = el.querySelector('a[href*="sr_id"], a[href*="careers/position"]');
       return { title: titleEl ? titleEl.innerText.trim() : '', url: urlEl ? urlEl.href : '' };
     });
     JSON.stringify(jobs);
     ```
   - If the above returns empty or fewer than 5 jobs, fall back to browser_snapshot and individually inspect links containing "careers/position"

## Step 3: Apply hard filters (from PREFERENCES.md)
Hard filters — any role failing these is excluded immediately:
- Bay Area onsite/hybrid only (Mountain View, San Jose, Palo Alto, Menlo Park, etc.)
- Confirmed people-management scope required — JD must explicitly mention managing, hiring, mentoring engineers, or having direct reports
- EM/Director level — no IC-only roles (Staff MLE, Senior MLE, Tech Lead without direct reports, Founding Engineer IC, etc.)
- Role families to prioritize: EM/Director for Agentic AI, Conversational AI, LLM Platform, RAG/Search, ML Infra

## Step 4: Score remaining roles
Score 1–100 using scoring-rubric.md. Top signals:
- Agentic AI, multi-agent systems, LLM orchestration, RAG, ranking/relevance, ML platform
- Scale (B+ users/queries handled)
- People management scope confirmed in JD
- Compensation bands (if publicly listed)

## Step 5: Inspect shortlisted candidates
For each role passing hard filters, navigate to its URL and verify:
- People management scope is confirmed (exact JD language preferred)
- Location/work model/comp are confirmed
- Top domain signals are present

## Step 6: Archive results
Save the shortlist to:
- ~/Documents/jobsearch/results/YYYY-MM-DD-moveworks.md (human-readable, use output-format.md template)
- ~/Documents/jobsearch/results/YYYY-MM-DD-moveworks.json (machine-readable, same structure as prior runs)

Replace YYYY-MM-DD with today's date.

## Step 7: Deliver to Telegram
Send the shortlist to Ratul via Telegram. Use target `telegram` (home channel). Format as a clean message:

```
📋 Moveworks Job Shortlist — [DATE]

🔍 Total roles reviewed: N → N shortlisted

[RANK 1] [TITLE] — Score: XX
• Department | Location | Work model | Comp
• Hard filters: ✅ / ❌
• Why it matches: 2-3 bullet points
• Risks: 1-2 bullet points
• Source: [URL]

[Additional shortlisted roles in same format]

---
Excluded: [reason] — N roles
Notes: [any notable friction points or changes from prior runs]
```

If no roles pass hard filters, send a message saying so and note any new IC-only roles observed.

## Important
- This is a scheduled automated run — do NOT ask questions or request clarification
- If the Moveworks page structure has changed and the extraction technique fails, try alternative selectors and document the change in the Notes section
- Produce both .md and .json archive files every run — overwrite any existing file for the same date
- Always deliver the Telegram message, even if the shortlist is empty
